key_insight: PINN training can match full-space optimization within a small Hessian eigensubspace selected by gradient alignment rather than eigenvalue magnitude.
engineering_relevance: Gradient-aligned subspaces could guide more targeted optimizers for ill-conditioned PDE learning problems without requiring well-conditioned projected curvature.
method: Select the dominant aligned subspace (DAS) by gradient alignment, not curvature magnitude.
Restrict training to DAS with line search and extend the analysis to Gauss–Newton.
evidence_signal: Across Poisson, heat, wave, and viscous Burgers benchmarks, DAS-restricted training empirically matches full-space training even when the projected Hessian remains ill-conditioned.
watch_item: Full Hessian eigendecomposition is costly at scale, and the abstract does not establish computational savings or generalization beyond the tested PINNs.
paper_title: A Systematic Analysis of a Small Optimal Subspace for Physics-Informed Neural Networks: $n$-DAS $\subset \mathbb{R}^p$
